items.summary: An open-source project from HKU that analyzes any software codebase through a 7-phase pipeline and auto-generates a dedicated CLI with --json output and a stateful REPL, plus a SKILL.md so agents can discover and call it themselves. Ready-made harnesses already cover Blender, GIMP, LibreOffice, FreeCAD, Obsidian and 100+ more apps, installable in one command from CLI-Hub. Apache-2.0, ~65k stars.
items.title: CLI-Anything: let coding agents drive desktop software without screenshots — auto-generated CLIs with --json output (No. 3 on GitHub Trending, Nov 20)

items.summary: A terminal coding agent that reads your repo, plans, and shows every edit as a diff for approval, then runs tests until they pass. Version 0.5.0 adds parallel subagents (each in its own git worktree), background agents that keep going after you close the terminal (omi bg), cloud agents that run on GitHub Actions and open a PR (omi cloud), and built-in browser testing that clicks through your app. 13 models to choose from, plus local models via Ollama; free allowance refills every 5 hours.
items.title: Omi CLI: the agent keeps working after you close the terminal — background and cloud agents that open PRs (No. 8 on Product Hunt, Nov 22)

items.summary: Isolated compute for AI agents: each agent code run starts in its own Firecracker microVM with its own kernel and is thrown away when done — a stronger boundary than a shared-kernel container. Persistent cloud workspaces, leasable build machines, and a way to plug in your own Linux or macOS lab hardware round it out. Connects via API, SDK or MCP to Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, with policies, human approvals and a hash-chained audit log; the free tier includes 100 awake vCPU-hours a month.
items.title: Sandscale: every agent code run gets its own Firecracker microVM with its own kernel — 100 hours free (Show HN, Nov 20)
